newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares finished the week down on Friday, but hectic trade saw the bourse post a new record in terms of turnover and stocks were seen moving firmly into next week.

The market took a slight knock from Wall Street-inspired falls on most global markets and comments from Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals that monetary policy may need to be tightened to curb credit growth.
But dealers said the trend of the market was still upward.
"It was a delayed reaction to Wall Street, but all it will do is slow our market's upward trend slightly. We are in a positive market," one dealer said.
The all-share index ended off 15.9 points at 7,072.0 and industrials lost 19.4 points to 8,406.0.

However, the day saw huge volumes of shares flowing through the market with a new record of 1.506 billion rands worth of stocks being traded. The previous high was 1.447 billion on February 13 earlier this year.
Volumes were boosted by a steady flow of asset swaps, most notably from tobacco concern Richemont Ltd, and the flotation of chicken restaurant Nando's Ltd.

More than three million Richemont shares were traded in an asset swap deal and SMK Securities, the brokers that did the swap, said it had been carried out in three tranches. They declined to give further details.
Richemont ended flat at 64.50 rand with 5.1 million shares trading. Experts predict more asset swaps in the market.

"There have been more (swaps) than before...possibly with the rand having stuck in a tight band for the last month or three, foreigners are feeling buoyant about doing asset swaps with us," said Greg Amoils, a director of portfolio management at Irish & Menell Rosenberg.

But Nando's was probably the feature of the day as the debutante stock ended at its opening price of 150 cents with more than 10.6 million shares trading. The price is a 50 percent jump on its issue price of 100 cents.

Nandos chief financial officer Bobby Favish said the listing was proceeding well. "We are very happy with the listing. We see it as a first step in the long journey to become a major player in the world," Favish told Reuters.
Another stock that attracted heavy interest were steel giant Iscor Ltd which saw 8.5 million shares traded amd ended up two cents at 307 cents.
Dealers said trade was helped by bookover deals of around 3.3 million shares and one buy order from an unnamed foreign institution for one million shares in the firm.
However, Toco Holdings Ltd fell 16 cents to 79 cents after a profit warning.
The gold index had a better day as bullion steadied and some buying crept into the market, but dealers said there were no signs of any major change in attitude to the battered counters.
"There was some buying, but that was about it," one dealer said.
Gold shares ended up 4.5 points to 1,235.0.
Near-dated gold futures contracts mirrored their spot market cousins and also ticked up. They were last at 880/889 from a settlement of 866.
However, June all-share contracts were off to 6,540/60 from 6,598 and the industrials contracts were at 8,215/25 from 8,305.
-- Paul Harris, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
